Windows MuPDF Static Libraries
===============================

This directory must contain the Windows static library files before the
SCHOLION_WITH_MUPDF build option can be enabled:

    mupdf.lib
    mupdf-third.lib

These are the Windows equivalents of the macOS libmupdf.a / libmupdf-third.a
files in ../scholion/third_party/mupdf/lib/.

The MuPDF header files are shared from:
    ../scholion/third_party/mupdf/include/

HOW TO OBTAIN THE WINDOWS LIBRARIES
-------------------------------------

Option A — Build MuPDF from source on Windows (recommended; version matches headers)
  1. Download MuPDF source from https://mupdf.com/downloads/
     Use the SAME version as the bundled macOS headers (check the version in
     ../scholion/third_party/mupdf/include/mupdf/fitz.h or the lib filenames).
  2. Open a Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt (x64).
  3. cd into the MuPDF source directory.
  4. Run:  nmake HAVE_X11=no HAVE_GLUT=no libs
     This builds libmupdf.lib and libmupdf-third.lib in the build/ directory.
  5. Copy them here and rename:
       libmupdf.lib      → mupdf.lib
       libmupdf-third.lib → mupdf-third.lib

  For MSYS2/MinGW, replace nmake with:
     make HAVE_X11=no HAVE_GLUT=no libs
  Output will be .a files; rename to .lib (MinGW accepts both extensions).

Option B — Use MuPDF prebuilt Windows release
  Download a Windows binary release from https://mupdf.com/downloads/ — look for
  a "windows" or "win64" variant. Extract the static libs and copy here.
  Verify the version matches the bundled headers before linking.

Option C — Swap to PDFium (avoids AGPL; harder to build)
  See CLAUDE.md section on PDFium migration — recommended only if distributing
  a closed-source binary.

VERIFYING THE BUILD
--------------------
After placing the libs, configure the Windows build with:
  cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSCHOLION_WITH_MUPDF=ON
If CMake reports FATAL_ERROR about missing mupdf.lib, the file is missing or
misnamed in this directory.
